work: 'Umdat al-salik wa 'uddat al-nasik (Reliance of the Traveller), Arabic facing text with English, Amana Publications (scan: islamicbulletin.com PDF)
author: Ahmad ibn al-Naqib al-Misri (text); edited and translated by Nuh Ha Mim Keller
date: Mamluk-era text (8th/14th c.); English tr. undated in scan
ref: Reliance o9.1, 'The obligatory character of jihad' (Keller numbering)
arabic_edition: Facing Arabic in the same PDF; OCR of the Arabic column is unusable, so left empty
english: Jihad is a communal obligation (def: c3.2). When enough people perform it to successfully accomplish it, it is no longer obligatory upon others ... The first is when they are in their own countries, in which case jihad (def: 09.8) is a communal obligation, and this is what our author is speaking of when he says, "Jihad is a communal obligation," meaning upon the Muslims each year.
what_it_says: Against non-Muslims in their own lands, jihad is a communal duty that the author means as due upon Muslims each year.

english: The caliph (025) makes war upon Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians (N: provided he has first invited them to enter Islam in faith and practice, and if they will not, then invited them to enter the social order of Islam by paying the non-Muslim poll tax (jizya, def: 011.4)-which is the significance of their paying it, not the money itself-while remaining in their ancestral religions) (O: and the war continues) until they become Muslim or else pay the non-Muslim poll tax

english: With respect to the hukm of this activity, the jurists agreed unanimously that it is a collective and not a universal obligation, except for 'Abd Allah Ibn al-Hasan who said it is voluntary. ... Its imposition as a communal obligation, that is, when some undertake it the rest are absolved of it, is based upon the words of the Exalted, "And the believers should not all go out to fight. Of every troop of them, a party only should go forth ..."

page: printed pp. 454-455 (running heads 'THE BOOK OF JIHAD 455')
what_it_says: Jihad is a collective obligation: when some undertake it the rest are excused.

work: Bidayat al-mujtahid wa nihayat al-muqtasid, 'The Distinguished Jurist's Primer' Vol. 1, Book of Jihad (scan: archive.org)
author: Ibn Rushd (Averroes), d. 595/1198 (general reference)
ref: Book of Jihad, 10.1.3 Section 3: harm permitted to the enemy; choices over prisoners
english: Harm that amounts to enslavement is permitted by way of consensus (ijma') for all categories of the polytheists, I mean, their men and women, old and young, and the common people and the elite with the exception of monks. ... The majority of the jurists maintained that the imam has different types of choices regarding the prisoners of war including their pardon, enslavement, execution, demand for ransom, and the imposition of jizya (poll tax) on them.
translator: Imran Ahsan Khan Nyazee (reviewed by Mohammad Abdul Rauf)
what_it_says: Enslavement of all categories of polytheists is agreed; the majority allow the imam to pardon, enslave, execute, ransom or impose jizya on prisoners.

work: Bidayat al-mujtahid wa nihayat al-muqtasid, 'The Distinguished Jurist's Primer' Vol. 1, Book of Jihad (scan: archive.org)
author: Ibn Rushd (Averroes), d. 595/1198 (general reference)
ref: Book of Jihad, 10.1.4 Section 4: the condition for the declaration of war (hadith on the three choices; footnote number not in OCR)
english: The condition for the declaration of war, by agreement, is the communication of the invitation to Islam, that is, it is not permitted to wage war on them unless the invitation has reached them. ... It has been established from the Prophet ... that he used to say to the commander upon sending a detachment, "When you come to face your enemy, the polytheists, invite them to opt for three choices ... Invite them to Islam, and if they agree refrain from attacking them ... If they refuse call on them to pay the jizya (poll tax). If they agree, accept it from them and refrain from (fighting) them, but if they refuse, seek support from Allah and fight them". It is, however, established from the Prophet ... that he used to ensnare the enemy and ambush them during the wars.
translator: Imran Ahsan Khan Nyazee (reviewed by Mohammad Abdul Rauf)
what_it_says: Invitation to Islam is a precondition of war; the hadith gives the Islam, then jizya, then fight sequence, while Ibn Rushd reports that jurists disagreed on whether invitation must be repeated and whether the Prophet's ambushes abrogated it.
memory_only: The hadith's collection (likely Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad) is not given in the OCR text; verify before citing.
